tasks.short: Forecast workforce supply, demand, costs, and hiring needs.

steps.what: Export employee, vacancy, absence, and pay baselines.
Supply approved budgets, workload forecasts, and cost assumptions.
Agree demand drivers, productivity assumptions, and plausible organisational changes with department managers.
Reconcile positions, working hours, cost centres, and conflicting snapshots.
Calculate workforce gaps, hiring dates, and costs under alternative assumptions.
Prepare the workforce proposal with recommended actions and unresolved trade-offs.
Challenge assumptions and approve workforce priorities and spending limits.

tasks.design: A scheduled integration on the {DATA_PLATFORM} reconciles {HCM}, {ATS}, {PAYROLL}, and {ERP} records using effective dates and shared identifiers. A deterministic scenario calculator feeds a {BI} view and a proposal template in {DOCS}; managers supply assumptions, choose recommendations, and approve spending.
tasks.previous_blocker: Different snapshots, inconsistent position identifiers, and local planning workbooks made repeatable calculations expensive to maintain. Demand assumptions still required management judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding reduces the effort to build adapters, reconciliation rules, scenario calculations, and document templates. No new forecasting breakthrough is assumed.
tasks.still_hard: Demand shocks, changing productivity, and uncertain organisational plans remain difficult to predict. Clean arithmetic cannot make weak assumptions reliable.
tasks.human_edge: The manager understands which shortages threaten delivery and negotiates credible trade-offs between hiring, redeployment, training, and workload.

ambition.what: Monthly decisions on the timing of critical-role recruitment.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time rebuilding forecasts and more time testing department assumptions. Within delegated budget limits, they can bring forward recruitment decisions using current scenarios.

reach.task: Model the cost of alternative workforce mixes.
reach.learn: Salary structures, employer costs, and cost sensitivity analysis.

evidence.claim: Structured workforce data supports deterministic reconciliation, scenario calculations, and templated reporting.
A study across 11 occupations including HR found modest average time savings; it does not validate these step estimates.

assumptions: This is a representative planning cycle in a company with 200 to 2,000 staff.
Time shares cover staff effort across the task, not calendar waiting time.
Forecasts use aggregate roles and teams; individual employment decisions remain separate.
Build ranges cover one planning model. Access and any consultation under national rules may extend elapsed delivery.
Step savings and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.
unknowns: Which systems contain authoritative positions, vacancies, budgets, and working hours?
Are shared identifiers and historical snapshots available?
Who may approve recruitment timing and workforce spending?
Which national consultation requirements and existing employee agreements apply?
research_questions: Which forecasting assumptions are supported by evidence for the relevant industry?
Which national rules apply if planning introduces individual-level employee analysis?
new_work: Resolve unmatched positions and inconsistent effective dates.
Maintain cost assumptions, workload drivers, and scenario formulas.
Compare forecasts with actual outcomes and investigate persistent errors.
Review access permissions and integration failures.

tasks.short: Track employment law, arbitration, and collective agreements to assess trends and organisational implications.

steps.what: Collect relevant legal updates, arbitration decisions, and collective agreement versions.
Read sources and record changes, dates, affected topics, and recurring industry themes.

loop.input: Versioned source documents and the previous change register.
loop.output: Proposed change entries with quotations, source locations, jurisdiction, legal status, dates, and uncertainty.
loop.check: Validate source locations and dates mechanically; the manager checks cited passages and distinctions between proposals and effective rules.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per document; missing passages, conflicting dates, or unreadable pages go to manual reading.
loop.why_not_simpler: Document retrieval and version comparison are deterministic; identifying relevant changes across varied legal prose needs bounded language interpretation.

steps.what: Assess applicability, industry patterns, and implications for employment policies.
Resolve material ambiguities and confirm interpretations that would change employment practice.
Approve a briefing containing trends, implications, actions, and source references.
Distribute the approved briefing and archive superseded material.

tasks.design: A source register in {DOCS} drives scheduled collection from approved {GOV_PORTAL} sources and subscribed updates in {EMAIL}. A bounded extraction loop proposes cited change entries, while deterministic templates assemble the briefing from reviewed entries and confirmed interpretations. Configured approval and distribution in {WORKFLOW} publish only approved material.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sources used inconsistent formats, and legal changes required interpretation across documents and versions. Generic search alerts could identify documents but could not establish their local implications.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded extraction can produce source-linked drafts from varied documents. Faster integration work makes version tracking, review queues, and publication controls practical for smaller HR teams.
tasks.still_hard: Applicability depends on jurisdiction, agreement coverage, facts, and legal interpretation. Source access, publication delays, and ambiguous decisions remain expensive.
tasks.human_edge: The manager distinguishes an interesting industry signal from a change that warrants advice, consultation, or action.

ambition.what: A monthly employment-change briefing for department managers with dated actions.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time collecting documents and more time interpreting implications with legal advisers. They can prioritise policy reviews, but gain no authority to settle disputed law.

reach.task: Translate collective agreement changes into operational guidance.
reach.learn: Agreement coverage, interpretive practice, and consultation procedures.

evidence.claim: Version tracking, source collection, and publication controls can be deterministic; legal applicability requires professional judgement.
GDPR restricts solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects on individuals.

assumptions: Monitoring covers a defined set of jurisdictions, agreements, and employment topics.
Legal advisers review material ambiguities rather than every routine update.
Sources are lawfully accessible; confidential disputes receive restricted access.
Build ranges cover an initial source set, not every European jurisdiction.
Time shares and remaining time are estimates; legal review effort varies with the material.
unknowns: Which jurisdictions and collective agreements cover the workforce?
Which subscriptions allow automated retrieval and processing?
Who provides legal advice, and what triggers mandatory review?
Which audiences may receive confidential arbitration material?
research_questions: Which official sources provide reliable version histories and publication feeds?
What are the current effective dates and legal status of relevant changes?
What reuse restrictions apply to the selected legal publications?
new_work: Maintain the source register and document access rights.
Check citations, dates, legal status, and extraction exceptions.
Remove duplicate updates and correct misleading trend entries.
Review extraction quality after source formats change.

tasks.short: Design, run, and evaluate HR programmes such as pay equity, childcare support, and employee awards.

steps.what: Agree the programme's purpose, target group, constraints, and success measures.
Gather the employee, pay, participation, and programme records needed for the brief.
Calculate coverage, costs, and relevant disparities under alternative programme rules.
Design programme options, eligibility criteria, safeguards, and delivery arrangements.
Consult employees, representatives, and delivery teams about proposed options.
Approve programme rules, funding, and launch conditions after required consultation.
Collect applications or nominations and prepare eligibility checks and proposed allocations.
Review exceptions and approve individual awards, benefits, or pay adjustments.
Record approved allocations and route delivery instructions to payroll or programme providers.
Evaluate participation, costs, outcomes, and complaints against the programme's aims.

tasks.design: A programme register in {PROJECT} holds the brief, approved rules, consultations, and decisions; configured forms and queues in {WORKFLOW} replace mailbox administration. Deterministic calculations join authorised {HCM} and {PAYROLL} data for scenarios and {BI} monitoring, while integrations deliver individually approved instructions. People retain programme design, consultation, disputed eligibility, and allocation decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each programme combined a different policy, approval chain, dataset, and delivery process. Small volumes rarely justified bespoke integrations and forms.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes reusable programme forms, rule tables, adapters, and dashboards cheaper to build. Existing workflow configuration can handle much of the administration without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Pay equity, childcare, and awards need different measures and safeguards. Statistical differences do not establish their causes, and participation does not prove programme impact.
tasks.human_edge: The manager designs a programme employees regard as fair, reconciles competing needs, and handles sensitive individual circumstances.

ambition.what: A childcare-support pilot accessible to shift workers.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends more time testing programme design with employees and less time chasing applications. They can propose bounded pilots within delegated funding; entitlement and pay decisions retain their existing approvals.

reach.role: Compensation, Benefits, and Job Analysis Specialists
reach.task: Investigate pay differences using job structures and defensible comparison groups.
reach.learn: Job evaluation, pay components, statistical limitations, and lawful data use.

evidence.claim: Forms, rule tables, approval queues, and delivery integrations can automate programme administration.
AFAS Profit 8 records job schemes for pay transparency; this supports one component, not the complete programme design.
Significant individual decisions require safeguards against solely automated decision-making.
Dutch works-council consent requirements cover specified pay, evaluation, and employee-data arrangements; other national rules vary.

assumptions: Steps represent one programme lifecycle; data and delivery branches vary by programme.
Build ranges cover one programme and reusable administration, not every programme listed.
Automatic routing uses explicit prior approval of the person, amount, recipient, and delivery instruction.
Actual payments retain the normal pay-cycle or procure-to-pay controls.
GDPR applies; sensitive analyses use lawful access, data minimisation, and restricted reporting.
Consultation ranges include employee or works-council processes where national rules require them; negotiations may take longer.
unknowns: Which programme is the first implementation?
Who can approve programme rules, individual allocations, and provider instructions?
What consultation, collective agreement, or national requirements apply?
Which employee groups currently face barriers to participation?
Which data may lawfully support pay-equity comparisons?
research_questions: Which evaluation method fits the chosen programme's intended outcome?
Which current national pay-transparency, tax, and benefits rules apply?
Which provider interfaces support acknowledged delivery and correction of instructions?
new_work: Maintain programme rules and versioned approval records.
Handle disputed eligibility, missing applications, and delivery failures.
Review small-group disclosure risks and reporting access.
Evaluate whether the programme improves outcomes rather than participation alone.
Update delivery mappings when benefits or providers change.

tasks.short: Develop, administer, and evaluate job-relevant applicant tests.

steps.what: Define job requirements, assessment purpose, and candidate accommodation needs with the hiring manager.
Select validated tests or develop job-relevant work samples and scoring rubrics.
Validate and approve the protocol using specialist review and evidence from the assessment platform {OTHER}.
Invite candidates through the assessment platform {OTHER} and explain timing, purpose, and support.
Monitor completion and resolve access problems and accommodation requests.
Consolidate objective scores and flag incomplete or irregular test records.
Interpret results, assess subjective responses, and approve a contextual assessment report.
Evaluate reliability, candidate experience, outcomes, and lawful group-level disparity measures.
Approve continued use, specialist revalidation, revision, or withdrawal of the assessment.

tasks.design: Configure invitations, reminders, completion records, and validated objective scoring in the assessment platform {OTHER}, linked to the {ATS}. Deterministic reporting in {BI} supports periodic evaluation with restricted access and minimum group sizes. Qualified people approve protocols, interpret results, and handle accommodations; hiring decisions remain with authorised people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Administration crossed the {ATS}, an assessment platform {OTHER}, and local reports. Test validity and interpretation required specialist expertise that automation could not replace.
tasks.enabler_now: Cheaper integration work can connect existing validated assessments, candidate support queues, and evaluation reports. Configuration handles routine administration without introducing model-based candidate scoring.
tasks.still_hard: Small hiring volumes limit statistical evaluation. Accessibility, test validity, changing job requirements, and interpreting individual results require specialist judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Qualified people judge whether a test measures relevant capability and whether a candidate's circumstances make the result misleading.

ambition.what: A quarterly assessment-quality review covering validity, accommodations, and candidate experience.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time coordinating tests and more time checking their usefulness and fairness. They gain a clearer basis to suspend a poor assessment within existing authority.

reach.task: Review assessment accessibility and investigate disparities in selection outcomes.
reach.learn: Lawful group analysis, reasonable accommodations, statistical uncertainty, and complaint handling.

evidence.claim: Assessment invitations, completion tracking, and consolidation of validated objective scores can use configuration and deterministic integration.
AI used to evaluate candidates falls within the employment uses listed in AI Act Annex III; deterministic administration alone does not establish that classification.
GDPR restricts solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects, including relevant employment decisions.
Reported hiring-AI litigation illustrates that employers retain responsibilities when procuring screening technology.

assumptions: The assessment platform category is represented by {OTHER} throughout.
An internal or external qualified assessment specialist supports the HR manager.
The initial implementation uses existing validated tests or work samples; new psychometric validation is outside the build estimate.
Candidate test-taking time is excluded from staff-effort shares.
The system does not automatically reject, rank, or select candidates.
Objective scoring uses the approved rubric; subjective interpretation remains human.
GDPR applies throughout; consultation and employment requirements depend on national rules.
unknowns: Which tests are used, and what validation evidence supports their intended use?
Are specialist qualifications or licences required for these tests?
Which interfaces and score-export rights are available?
How are accommodations requested, approved, and recorded?
What lawful data and sufficient sample sizes exist for evaluation?
Does the existing assessment platform contain AI-based evaluation features?
research_questions: What evidence supports validity and accessibility for the intended jobs and languages?
Which current EU AI Act obligations apply to any AI assessment features actually used?
Which national rules govern testing, employee consultation, and sensitive assessment data?
Which evaluation measures remain meaningful at the expected hiring volumes?
new_work: Maintain approved protocols, rubric versions, and integration mappings.
Handle delivery failures, incomplete records, and accommodation requests.
Review evaluation dashboards with a qualified specialist.
Investigate complaints and unexplained outcome differences.
Revalidate or withdraw tests when jobs or assessment conditions change.

role.altitude: The HR manager spends less of the week assembling records, chasing programme administration, and rebuilding reports. More time goes to workforce trade-offs, employee consultation, legal interpretation, and assessment quality; decision rights change only through explicit delegation.
reach: Workforce cost modelling with Compensation and Benefits Managers.
Collective agreement interpretation with Labor Relations Specialists.
Pay-equity investigation with Compensation, Benefits, and Job Analysis Specialists.
Assessment accessibility and outcome review with Equal Opportunity Representatives and Officers.
skills_to_grow: Scenario design and interpretation of forecast uncertainty.
Data definitions, reconciliation, and access governance.
Source verification and recognition of legal ambiguity.
Assessment validity, accessibility, and statistical limitations.
role.ambitious_version: Run a recurring workforce and programme review that joins current capacity scenarios, employee needs, programme outcomes, and assessment quality. Bring specific decisions to authorised leaders while preserving direct access to HR for sensitive cases.
